candidates.angle: reserve — (R) Reservation: every agent carves an ops (data/execution) sub-mandate from its own reservation; trading capital = available(agent); every allocator move respects reserved-vs-available; stop-out = one tree.close; deliberate freed-capital policy; reservation invariants checked after every write and every tick.
candidates.hypothesis: Structure, not a return claim. (R) Each agent's reservation = trading capital + an ops child mandate `ops.<agent>` (1% of trading capital, purposes data/execution, merchants = the agent's instruments) that it pays from through core pay(). The book trades available(agent) (budget - spentDirect - reserved), so the allocator can never size or trade capital that is reserved below an agent or already spent. Allocator moves (rebalance, crowding cut, ladder cut) go through Reservations.apply: shrink ops -> shrink agents -> pods settle to exactly their agents (freed = fund cash) -> grow pods -> grow agents -> grow ops; shrinks never go below committed (ops floored at spent), growth is paid only from fund cash and scaled uniformly if the fund cannot back it; deployable is additionally clamped to grantableTrading() = (root - everything spent anywhere)/(1+opsRate). (C) Stop-out = ONE tree.close(agent): the agent's trading capital AND unspent ops budget come back in one operation, subtree revoked (ops dies through the chain), subtree keeps exactly what it spent; the pod returns the freed authority to fund cash. Freed-capital policy: stop-out capital is fund cash until the next scheduled rebalance redeploys it by score; cut capital stays cash while the cut holds; spent ops authority is gone for good. Rules R1-R5 are checked exactly (bigint) after every write and at the end of every tick; the run stops (ReservationError) on any violation. Ops spend is a pass-through expense reported per agent and never enters trading NAV, so book returns are measured exactly as before. Expected utility effect: exactly zero (no arena agent spends, and the new constraints never bind at deploy 0.8 + 1% ops).
reviewProblems: The patch's central structural guarantee is false, and its test only passes because of rounding luck. The claim is that the allocator is only handed what the fund can reserve, and that the equal start is sized so the tree never refuses a move. book.ts computes `perAgent = Math.min(aum*deploy, toUsdc(res.grantableTrading())) / n` and then `toUnits(perAgent)`. That rounds half-up to 6 decimals, and `openAgent` adds `floor(trading*ppm/PPM)` of ops. When the clamp binds, n × (trading + ops) can exceed the AUM by up to n units. The last `openAgent` then throws `AttenuationError` (BUDGET_EXCEEDS_AVAILABLE) from `tree.resize(pod, ...)` in reserve.ts:143, and the whole `runBook` dies.

Concrete repro at the default deploy 0.8 through the new public `SwarmSpec.opsBudget` knob. With aum 10M, one pod and 11 TrendStrategy agents, `runBook` throws 'growth 909090909091 exceeds parent "fund.eth" available 909090909090' for opsBudget 0.25, 0.3 and 0.5. With opsBudget 0.25 it also throws for n=13 and n=14, and with 0.3 for n=14.

Concrete repro with the default 1% ops. A 13-agent roster at deploy 0.995 or 1 throws 'growth 769230769231 exceeds parent "fund.eth" available 769230769228' under both policies. On arena research seeds 1–100, deploy 0.995 crashes 70/200 runs, against 3/200 on HEAD. Two of those 70 are naive-policy runs that HEAD handled without error.

The test that is supposed to prove the guarantee is 'when ops budgets make authority binding, the allocator is only ever handed what the fund can reserve'. It runs deploy 1 with ops 0.3 and a 7-agent roster, where the rounding happens to go down. So it does not prove the guarantee: an 11-agent roster in the same setup fails. The same applies to the unconditional claims 'Every move is valid at every step, so the tree never rejects one' and that no growth needs clipping at write time. A fix would floor the per-agent trading in bigint (`grantable / BigInt(n)`) or let `openAgent` clip to what the fund has available, plus a test over many roster sizes.

Minor, inaccurate docs: the docs say the rules are 'checked exactly after every write', but ops `pay()` writes are only checked at the end of the tick. book.ts says ops spend 'never touches trading capital', yet spent ops permanently reduce `grantableTrading()` and therefore future deployable capital once the clamp binds; the patch's own deploy-1 test shows this. NAV is also never debited for the USDC actually paid to vendors, so reported returns do not include the ops expense.
Minor: the arena runs about 30% slower (60 worlds: 2.1s to 2.7s) because the full O(nodes) `violations()` scan now runs after every apply, close and tick.

Checked, no problem found: the diff applies cleanly to HEAD f5b2d80, and all 8 post-image blob hashes match the diff's index lines. `tsc -b` passes and `npm test` passes 201/201. The arena, judge and setup files are not touched. No test is weakened or removed. Nothing is hard-coded per seed. There is no look-ahead: `opsSpend` receives the same point-in-time Observation as `decide`. At the arena's deploy 0.8 with 1% ops, NAV, per-agent capital, decisions (t, kind, node) and ladder states are bit-identical to HEAD for 300 research worlds under both policies. The 60-world arena summary is bit-identical as well, so the zero-utility claim holds at arena settings.
candidates.reviewSummary: REJECT. The diff applies cleanly to HEAD: I reproduced all 8 files byte-for-byte in /tmp/loop-review-1-reserve/wt, and every blob hash matches the diff's index lines. Typecheck passes, 201/201 tests pass, and at arena settings (deploy 0.8, 1% ops) the change is bit-identical to HEAD across 300 research worlds under both policies. So the zero-utility claim holds, there is no look-ahead, and no judge files are touched. It still fails the structure bar, because the guarantee it sells is false. It claims the allocator and the initial equal start are only handed what the fund can reserve, and that the tree never refuses a move. In fact the initial allocation rounds `grantableTrading()/n` half-up to 6 decimals. Whenever the clamp binds, `Reservations.openAgent` then throws `AttenuationError` and `runBook` crashes. Examples: an 11-agent roster at the default deploy 0.8 with opsBudget 0.25, 0.3 or 0.5; a 13-agent roster at deploy 0.995 or 1 with the default 1% ops; and 70 of 200 arena runs at deploy 0.995, against 3 on HEAD. The patch's own test for this guarantee (deploy 1, ops 0.3) passes only because its 7-agent roster happens to round down, so it does not prove the claim. Fix by flooring the per-agent trading in bigint (or clipping in `openAgent`) and testing many roster sizes. Minor points: the 'checked after every write' wording skips `pay()`; 'never touches trading capital' is wrong once spent ops shrink `grantableTrading()`; NAV is not debited for ops payments; the arena runs about 30% slower. The scratch worktree with the patch applied is /tmp/loop-review-1-reserve/wt.

candidates.angle: (A) Risk-adjusted resizing, drawdown-aware: the drawdown ladder (cut to x0.5, stop-out) now measures an agent's drawdown against the vol that agent runs, not as a fixed percentage.
candidates.hypothesis:
The fixed 20% stop-out was the biggest leak in how records turn into capital. An agent's unit returns include 2x leverage and have 0.3–0.65 annual vol, so a 20% drawdown is about half a sigma. In the arena that stopped 8.2 of 9.7 agents per world on the old default, including 80% of skilled pickers (334/417) and desks (163/188). Deployed capital fell from 80% to 26% of deployable by year end.

A drawdown only says something about skill relative to the agent's risk. For a Sharpe-S agent the drawdown is roughly exponential, so P(dd ≥ kσ) ≈ e^(−2Sk). The fix scales every rung by max(1, ddStopVol·σ/ddStop), with ddStopVol = 1.5. For a Sharpe-1 agent that means about a 5% chance of sitting at the stop at any time, so revocation needs real evidence. σ is measured over the window up to the agent's last high-water mark. That way a crash cannot inflate its own yardstick and loosen its own stop.

The fixed percentages stay as floors. So the center book never cuts or stops an agent sooner than the agent's own stop-loss would. The per-agent guardrail baseline (naive) keeps its fixed stop.

Result: stop-outs fall to 2.5 per world and become selective. About 12% of pickers are stopped, versus 37% of trend agents, 46% of herders and 31% of rogues.
reviewProblems: Not blocking. The widening has no ceiling. scale = max(1, 1.5·σ/0.2) is unbounded, so any agent with σ ≥ 0.667 gets ddStop ≥ 100% and can never be stopped out. On research seeds 1–60, 82 of 570 agents hit this at some tick. Of the 396 cases where the risk-scaled rung overrode the fixed 20% stop, 27 had the stop at 100% or more. Rogue agents rode drawdowns of 74–93% without revocation: seed 34 rogue (maxDD 93%), seed 41 rogue (91%), seed 22 rogue (81%). Rogue stop-outs fell from 31/31 to 10/31. Suggested fix: cap scale, or cap ddStop below 1 (e.g. min(ddStopMax, ·)).

Not blocking. σ has no minimum sample size. volAtHighWater takes whatever returns lie before the high-water mark, even 2 or 3 of them. Across the 396 overrides, 40 used σ from fewer than 10 observations and 16 from fewer than 5. Seed 10 noise-0 got a 106% stop from 2 observations; seed 41 rogue got a 114% stop from 6. Synthetic case: [0.05, 0.001, then -0.004 per day] → σ 55%, stop 82.5%, and a 55% drawdown is only cut. Because of max(1, ·), estimation noise only ever loosens the stop. That contradicts the comment that 'revocation needs real evidence'. Suggested fix: require n ≥ warmup observations (or shrink σ toward the fixed rung).

Not blocking. The 'cannot loosen its own limit' guarantee is one-sided. The return that SETS the high-water mark is always inside the σ window, so one lucky up-jump (such as an earnings print) inflates σ and loosens the limit for every loss after it. Case: 60 calm ticks (σ≈8%), one +25% tick, then -1%/day. σ becomes 51% and the stop 77%, so a 45% drawdown is only cut. The tests only prove the crash direction.

Not blocking. The documented invariant and published numbers go stale. docs/CENTER-BOOK.md says both books 'share agents, gate, leverage, initial capital and stop-out rule; they differ only in whether anything looks across the agents'. The center book now overrides each agent's own 20% stop with a looser one, which is a per-agent rule change and not a cross-agent one. Much of the uplift over naive therefore comes from giving only the center book the looser stop. README.md:90 ('revoke at 20%'), docs/CENTER-BOOK.md:99 and its demo:swarm results/ablation numbers are not updated. services/orchestrator/src/agenthire-demo.ts:589-593 still presents the fixed rungs as 'center-book defaults'.

Not blocking. Book-level max drawdown gets worse. On seeds 3000–3149 the center book's mean maxDD rises from 6.6% to 7.9%, above the naive baseline's 6.9%. Utility and Sharpe still improve (Sharpe 0.70 → 1.05).

Minor. The random-records check that scaled rungs dominate the fixed ones is a tautology given max(1, ·). book.ts passes an already-scaled ScaledLadder into nextLadderState, which scales again. That is only safe because ScaledLadder has no ddStopVol field, which is fragile. volAtHighWater uses e >= peak while currentDrawdown uses e > peak (harmless here).
candidates.reviewSummary:
Verdict: accept (ok = true). None of the reject criteria apply, but several robustness gaps should be fixed. The diff applies cleanly to HEAD f5b2d80 in /tmp/loop-review-1-resize/wt. `tsc -b` passes and `npm test` passes 191/191: three new tests, no existing test deleted or weakened.

Checks against the reject criteria:
- **Future data:** none read. σ is computed only from the agent's realized unitReturns up to tick t, in step 6 after the tick-t close. The window is center.window = 90, not whole-sample.
- **Strategy class or internals:** not used; the mechanism reads realized vol only.
- **Arena/judge files:** none edited.
- **Seed-specific constants:** none in production code; ddStopVol = 1.5 is a general parameter.
- **Guarantee proven:** ddStopVol = 0 reproduces the fixed ladder's stop-outs exactly (tested). The floor guarantee (never stopped sooner than naive) is tested.

The claims reproduce:
- **Research seeds 1–60:** stop-outs fall from 7.95 to 2.45 per world. Pickers drop from 102/123 to 9/123 and desks from 44/55 to 4/55. Deployed capital at year end rises from 20% to 56% of deployable. Utility vs the fixed ladder is +6.8pp (90% CI 4.6–9.1).
- **Out of sample, arena CLI on seeds 3000–3149:** allocator utility is +4.1pp vs HEAD (CI 3.1–5.1, 68% of worlds better). Tiger is unchanged.

The problems are loosened risk control, not leakage or cheating:
- **No ceiling:** the widening is unbounded, so about 14% of agents at some point have a stop at 100% or more. That includes rogues that ran to 74–93% drawdowns without revocation.
- **Tiny samples:** σ can come from 2–6 observations, and max(1, ·) turns that noise into looser stops.
- **Up-jumps:** a single up-jump that sets the high-water mark inflates σ.
- **Stale docs:** the docs still say both books share the stop-out rule.

Recommended follow-ups:
- cap the scale or ddStop;
- require a minimum number of observations for σ;
- update README.md and docs/CENTER-BOOK.md.

candidates.angle: (G) Group cuts by operator. The center book's drawdown ladder now runs per COUNTERPARTY (AgentSpec.operator) instead of per agent name. All agents of one operator share one ladder state and are cut, restored and stopped out together. A stop-out closes every mandate the operator holds in one step (tree.close on each member, then the pods shrink; delegated sub-budgets are reclaimed too). The counterparty's record is capital-weighted: the return on the capital the fund actually had with that operator, the pod-shop rule for a PM running several books. When nothing is funded it falls back to the equal-weight blend. A group of one is judged exactly as before.
candidates.hypothesis: An operator is one counterparty, so the risk decision (cut/stop) belongs to the operator, not to each name. This gives two things. (1) Sybil-proof stop-outs: no operator keeps trading under a second name after being stopped, and per-agent guardrails cannot do this. (2) A counterparty running two partly independent books is judged on the combined P&L of the fund's money with it, not killed by one book's noise. Capital weighting (rather than equal-weight pooling) closes a loophole: without it, an operator could hide a funded losing agent from the stop behind an unfunded mirror agent. Utility claim: none. Dev shows a significant gain but the check block does not confirm it, so this is submitted as STRUCTURE (a tested guarantee that does not reduce utility).
reviewProblems: Headline guarantee overclaimed; the diff opens a second-name shield against stop-outs. Replacing each agent's own record with a capital-weighted counterparty record (book.ts step 6, `counterpartyRecord`) drops HEAD's per-name stop for any agent that shares an operator. A losing name is no longer stopped at ddStop while a FUNDED co-operated name keeps the combined record above it. Capital weighting only closes the UNFUNDED-mirror case. Since the allocator funds any name with positive recent Sharpe, a funded shield is the realistic case. Repro on genericMarketConfig(7): operator 'mallory' runs NoiseStrategy(3) plus TrendStrategy(30), with unrelated TrendStrategy(30) and MeanReversionStrategy(3) agents. At HEAD the noise agent is stopped at t=74, when its own drawdown hits 20%. With the diff it stays funded for 15 more ticks at up to 1,000,000 USDC, loses 84k more, and is not stopped until t=185. Fund final NAV is 10,030,280 vs 10,202,135 at HEAD (-1.7%), and book maxDD is 5.62% vs 4.93%. No test covers or bounds this. Both-direction sybil-proofing ('any name stopped → all names stopped', with each name also still judged on its own record) would give the claimed guarantee without weakening HEAD.

The diff's own fixture shows the regression. In the new test 'an operator's agents move through the ladder together' (herd-a and herd-b under op-herd), herd-b's own drawdown reaches 20% at t=72. At HEAD it is stopped there. With the diff it keeps up to 411,941 USDC, its own drawdown reaches 59%, and it loses a further 108,458 USDC before the group stop at t=185. The test asserts that the two names move in lockstep, not that this is safe.

The book-level test 'an unfunded mirror agent cannot shield its operator from the stop-out' does not exercise the scenario it names. At the stop tick (t=122), yolo has 0 capital and the 'mirror' is the funded, losing leg: 992,651 USDC, own drawdown 24%. The stop comes from the allocator switching capital between the two legs after the t=30 reallocation (yolo funded, mirror 0) and back later, so the fund loses on both legs. It does not come from a funded loser being judged while its mirror is unfunded. Only the unit test in allocator.test.ts demonstrates the claimed property.

The utility neutrality holds only because of how the arena builds its rosters. In packages/lab/src/arena.ts, only SkilledPicker pairs (picker-i and desk-i) ever share an operator. On dev seeds 1–400 (HEAD vs candidate, paired), 263 of 400 worlds change, all of them worlds with shared operators. Per-world CE swings range from -19.3pp to +25.7pp. The mean gain (+0.56pp; +0.42pp on seeds 2000–2999) comes from the relaxation: across 264 worlds with shared operators, there are 311 cases of a grouped skilled picker still trading after its own record passed ddStop (16,513 funded ticks, +36.5M PnL, own drawdown up to 52%). In effect the arena's operator label marks skilled agents, so labelling this 'structure' merges a large, unconfirmed policy change under the no-harm bar. With adversarial shared operators (the threat model the proposal is about), the effect goes the other way, as the NoiseStrategy/TrendStrategy example in problem 1 shows.

The test 'agents with no shared operator are judged one by one, exactly as with no operators at all' compares new code against new code, not against HEAD. The stop path also changed from resize-to-0 plus revoke to tree.close followed by a pod shrink, which changes the tree event log (REVOKE now carries the freed amount and comes before the pod RESIZE). NAV equivalence with HEAD holds empirically: 0 of 136 dev worlds without shared operators changed. It is not tested.

Minor: when every member of a group has 0 capital, `counterpartyRecord` falls back to an equal-weight blend. There a mirror pair nets to 0 and stops accruing drawdown, which contradicts the docstring's statement that an unfunded agent 'cannot offset' another. Low impact, because both legs of a mirror pair are rarely unfunded at the same time.

Checks that pass: the diff applies cleanly to HEAD f5b2d80; all 196 tests and `tsc -b` pass; it is point-in-time (capital[k] and unitReturns[k] are both known at step 6 of tick k); no arena or judge files are touched; no tests are weakened; no seed-specific constants are in the mechanism. With grouping disabled, the 3 new runBook tests fail, so they do discriminate.
candidates.reviewSummary: REJECT. The diff applies cleanly to HEAD. All 196 tests and the typecheck pass, the mechanism is point-in-time, and it does not touch the arena or judge. The literal guarantee holds and is tested: once an operator is stopped, all of its names stop on the same tick and hold no capital afterwards. But this is not a pure structural tightening. Judging a group on one capital-weighted combined record removes HEAD's per-name stop-out for grouped agents, so a second, funded name can now keep a losing name trading past ddStop. Demonstrated: a noise agent that HEAD stops at t=74 runs to t=185, and the fund ends 1.7% lower. In the diff's own herd fixture, herd-b trades 113 ticks past its own stop, reaching 59% drawdown and losing 108k. The book-level mirror test's stop fires while the 'mirror' is the funded, losing leg, so it does not show what its title claims. The dev utility gain (+0.4 to +0.6pp, with per-world swings of -19 to +26pp) comes entirely from the arena pairing only skilled pickers under shared operators, which lets them avoid their individual stop-outs. So the 'does not reduce utility' argument depends on how the arena builds rosters, not on the guarantee. Scratch worktrees under /tmp/loop-review-1-group/ were created for testing and have been removed; the diff used is at /tmp/loop-review-1-group/group.diff.

candidates.angle: (C) Stop-out closes the subtree: book.ts stop-outs via DelegationTree.close with agents holding delegated sub-budgets; tree reservation/close invariants audited every tick; drawdown ladder redesigned (cut rung opt-in, stop rung kept).
candidates.hypothesis: Structure: a stop-out must take back the agent's capital AND every budget it delegated in one tree operation, and the book must never trade on a tree that breaks reservation (children <= parent, available >= 0) or strands authority under a revoked node. The old stop-out (applyTargets to 0 + revoke) cannot do this: resize(agent, 0) throws BELOW_COMMITTED as soon as the agent holds a sub-budget. Allocator: the drawdown CUT rung (x0.5 at 10% DD, restored only after recovering to 5%) is a trailing stop on the agent's own unit returns. It sells after losses and buys back after gains, while shrunk-Sharpe scoring already de-weights a PM whose record is deteriorating. So it should cost CE utility, and removing it should raise the fund's CRRA certainty equivalent. The stop rung stays.
reviewProblems: Non-blocking, test coverage moved: packages/swarm/src/book.test.ts 'the mandate tree stays valid through every reallocation, cut and stop-out' runs defaultCenterBookPolicy(). On seed 7 at HEAD that run made 7 CUT and 3 RESTORE decisions. With the new default it makes 0 of each. The file is not edited, but it no longer covers cuts, and its title and README row still say 'cut'. The cut path is still covered by close.test.ts ('center book with a cut rung', which asserts a CUT on the doomed agent and checks invariants every tick). RESTORE is not asserted anywhere at book level any more.

Non-blocking, overclaim: the docs say the book 'throws BookInvariantError rather than trading on a broken tree', but runBook calls options.onTick at the start of tick t and runs audit(t) only at the end. So anything onTick breaks (a direct write, or an unserialized overspend by sub-mandates) is allocated and marked to market for that tick first. close.test.ts asserts this lag itself (e.t === 40 for a break made at t=40). In the simulation the throw discards the result, so it has no effect. It would be exact if audit also ran right after onTick.

Non-blocking: close.test.ts DoomedStrategy.decide reads this.m.ticks[obs.t].returns, i.e. it looks ahead at the tick it trades into. It is a clearly labelled test fixture that forces a stop-out, and nothing the allocator or book uses depends on it: the ladder and scores still see only realized unitReturns. So this is not a lookahead in the mechanism.

Non-blocking: the slice check in close.test.ts skips any tick where the agent's budget is below 10x what its subtree has spent (a heuristic cutoff, not exact). The README row's 'sub-mandates stay their share of the PM' is therefore only checked away from those floor-bound cases (slicesChecked >= 200).

Non-blocking, modelling: capitalOf is the agent's whole budget, including sub-mandate reservations and their spent floors. applyTargets keeps max(target, floor), so when sub-mandates have spent a lot, a crowding cut can leave an agent above its crowd cap. This does not affect the arena, which has no sub-mandates.

Non-blocking, stale docs: the ablation table in docs/CENTER-BOOK.md (which still has a '− drawdown cut rung' row, while evaluate.ts now has '+ drawdown cut'), the README headline numbers and the checked-in apps/web/public/swarm-snapshot.json were all measured with the old cut-on default. The docs say so ('measured with it on').
candidates.reviewSummary:
Verdict: accept. None of the rejection criteria apply.

1. **Applies cleanly.** A scratch worktree of HEAD f5b2d80 is at /tmp/loop-review-1-close/wt. The patch applied without conflicts, and every file it produces has exactly the content ID the diff's `index` lines state (e.g. book.ts 2cfa5f3, close.test.ts 7330983, tree.ts d75c558, README ae90979).
2. **Builds and passes.** `tsc -b` is clean. `npm test` passes 201/201.
3. **Nothing forbidden touched.** It does not edit arena.ts, arena-cli.ts, loop-judge.mjs or worktree-setup.sh. Existing tests are not edited, skipped or deleted; only new tests are added.
4. **Point-in-time, not seed-specific, no strategy-class peeking.** The stop-out is `tree.close` at the stop tick, and the ladder uses realized unitReturns only. No seeds are hard-coded, and no skill is inferred from strategy classes.

**Do the structural tests prove the claim?** Yes. I broke the code six ways and checked that the tests fail each time (tree, book, close and allocator test files):
- Stop-out as a bare revoke: 10 failures.
- End-of-tick audit removed: the broken-tree test fails.
- The delegate refusal under a revoked ancestor removed: 5 failures.
- Sub-mandates never resized: 4 failures.
- The not-closed check removed from the book audit: 1 failure.
- The over-committed check removed from `audit()`: 3 failures.

The premise also holds: at HEAD, `resize(agent, 0)` throws BELOW_COMMITTED whenever the agent has handed out a sub-budget.

**Utility claim.** It reproduces exactly and holds on research seeds nobody cited. All figures are the centre book's CE utility change versus HEAD, paired, 90% CI; seeds ≥10000 were not touched.

| Seeds | Change | 90% CI | Note |

- The Tiger track is unchanged (difference 0), and so

candidates.angle: Risk-scaled drawdown ladder. The center book's cut and stop-out thresholds are now set in units of each agent's own volatility, instead of the fixed 10%/20% applied to every agent whatever risk it runs.
candidates.hypothesis: Diagnosis on dev seeds 401-600 (baseline code): the fixed ladder stops out most of the fund's best agents. Arena agents run 30-78% annual vol on their attributable (unit) record. At that vol a 20% drawdown is ordinary noise, so 80% of skilled pickers (unit Sharpe 1.1, unit mu +50%/yr) were revoked, at mean tick 94. There were 8.2 stop-outs per world, and after the stop-outs the book held only 35% of NAV deployed and ran about 8% vol. Removing the stop outright (diagnostic ablation, center only) was worth +4.3pp CE, and removing both rungs +5.4pp. Deleting stop-outs would contradict product point (C), so the ladder is kept and made risk-adjusted instead, as pod shops set drawdown limits relative to a PM's risk budget. The existing 10%/20% are read as 1 sigma / 2 sigma limits for an agent running 10% vol (new policy field ladderVol = 0.10, the only new number, chosen because it maps both existing thresholds to whole sigmas; it was not swept). An agent that runs hotter gets all three thresholds (ddCut, ddRecover, ddStop) multiplied by max(1, peakVol / ladderVol), so no threshold ever gets tighter than the fixed one. peakVol is the annualized vol of the agent's own unit returns over the trailing `window` returns ending at its high-water mark (or its first `warmup` returns if it peaked earlier). As a result the loss being judged is not in the sample and a crash day cannot loosen its own stop, and the limits stay frozen during a drawdown. With fewer than `warmup` returns the fixed percentages apply. Everything is point-in-time: only the agent's attributable returns through close t are used. There are no market reads, no skill labels and no strategy internals. The per-agent guardrail baseline keeps its fixed 20% stop.
reviewProblems: The claimed guarantee that 'the loss being judged is not in the sample, so a crash day cannot loosen its own stop' is false (it appears in the claim, the new docs/CENTER-BOOK.md text and the allocator test title). In effectiveLadder, `end = Math.max(peakAt + 1, minObs)`. When the high-water mark falls inside the first `warmup` = 30 returns, or the agent was never above water (peakAt = -1), the vol sample includes the post-peak losses being judged. Counterexample: 29 returns of ±0.1%, then −19% on the 30th. The scale jumps from 1.00 to 5.51 and ddStop from 20% to 110%. After 60 further −1% days (drawdown 55.7%) the agent is never stopped; the fixed ladder stops it at tick 31. On dev seeds 401–600, 369 of the 1,391 fixed-stop ticks the proposal lets through rely on a sample containing those post-peak losses. The test 'the losses being judged never loosen their own limit' only covers a peak after warmup, and the 'early peak' test asserts the exception as intended, so the tests do not prove the guarantee.

The scale has no cap, so the proposal quietly removes the stop-out for hot agents, which the claim itself says would contradict product point (C). ddStop is 2 × peakVol, so any agent measured at 50% vol or more has a stop at a drawdown of 100% or more. That cannot be reached at 2× leverage with gross ≤ 1. On dev seeds 401–600: the end-of-run scale has median 3.74 (stop at 75%), p90 6.42 (stop at 128%) and max 15.7. 569 of 1,930 agents (29%) had an unreachable stop at some tick, covering 19.4% of post-warmup agent-ticks. 394 agents reached a 50% unit drawdown; 269 were not stopped when they crossed it, and 129 of those still held capital. 81 of the 129 agents that reached 70% were not stopped by then; the worst drawdown was 95.9%.

The gain is mostly the stop-deletion ablation, repackaged. Stop-outs fall from 8.21 to 1.66 per world. CE rises +4.71pp (SE 0.62) over the fixed ladder, against +4.26pp for simply deleting the stop, which is the variant the researcher calls a contradiction of product point (C). No test checks that a stop stays reachable for a high-vol agent: the 'persistent bleed' test uses a ~40%-vol agent (stop at 80%) and needs 600 days of −0.4% returns to reach it.

The loosening is not targeted at skill as the diagnosis suggests. Stop-outs, fixed → proposal, on 401–600: noise (zero-edge) 238→27 of 297, picker 334→51 of 417, herd 227→41 of 227, rogue 105→57 of 106. Using only realized vol is legitimate, but the change is a blanket loosening for everyone, not a rescue of skilled pickers.

ddRecover is scaled by the same factor, up to about 15×. An agent cut under the fixed percentages before warmup is RESTOREd when its scale jumps at tick `warmup`, with no recovery at all: for example, cut at 12% drawdown, scale 4, ddRecover becomes 20%. The docs still say restore happens 'once it recovers to within 5% of its high-water mark'.

Artifacts left stale. The checked-in apps/web/public/swarm-snapshot.json is regenerated byte-identically by `npm run demo:swarm` at HEAD, but changes under this diff and the new version is not included, so the dashboard would show fixed-ladder results. services/orchestrator/src/agenthire-demo.ts and docs/AGENTHIRE.md still call the fixed 10%/20% ladder the 'center-book defaults'.

Suggested fix: cap the scaled stop (e.g. ddStop ≤ 50%, or scale ≤ 2.5). Measure vol only over returns up to the peak and require at least minObs of them, falling back to the fixed percentages otherwise. Leave ddRecover unscaled. Add a test that an agent at 60% vol or more is still stopped at a reachable drawdown.
candidates.reviewSummary: Verdict: reject. None of the listed gates fail, but the proposal's premise ('the ladder is kept') and its main guarantee do not hold in the arena. What checks out: the diff applies cleanly to HEAD f5b2d80; the post-image blob hashes match worktree .claude/worktrees/wf_ea873221-3e2-5, and it was applied to /tmp/loop-review-1-wildcard/wt. tsc -b passes. npm test passes 192/192 (188 at base plus 4 new; only import lines were removed from tests), with swarm 25/25 and lab 35/35. The arena, arena-cli, judge and worktree-setup are untouched. There is no identification of agents by strategy class and no seed-specific constant in the mechanism. Point-in-time is verified: truncating the market after tick k left every decision, capital and NAV before k unchanged in 120 of 120 cases (/tmp/loop-review-1-wildcard/pit.mts). The CENTER-BOOK.md numbers reproduce with demo:swarm, and the researcher's dev-seed diagnosis reproduces (8.21 stops per world; ablations +4.26pp and +5.43pp). What fails: (1) the stop scales without a cap as 2 × vol, so it cannot be reached for agents at 50% vol or more; 29% of dev-seed agents had an unreachable stop at some point, 269 of 394 agents with a 50% unit drawdown were not stopped by then, and the +4.71pp CE gain is about the same as the stop-deletion ablation the researcher says contradicts product point (C). (2) 'A crash cannot loosen its own stop' is false when the high-water mark is inside the first warmup returns: a concrete counterexample takes ddStop from 20% to 110%, 369 of the 1,391 stops waved through rely on this, and the tests do not prove the guarantee. Minor issues: ddRecover is scaled up to about 15× (restore with no recovery), and swarm-snapshot.json and the AgentHire docs/demo are left stale. Scratch scripts: /tmp/loop-review-1-wildcard/analyze.mts, loosen.mts, precise.mts, deep.mts.
